note: J44: transcripts for starting, steering, watching and answering a session from the domovoi command, with an exit code table. The transcripts themselves, the exit codes and the new-strings list live in the design's data; the owner questions are annotations.
annotations: Starting, steering, watching and answering a session

Transcripts for the four session commands. Each block is drawn at a fixed column width. The dashed line marks the last column, and each header reports the longest line so the test is visible. Amber appears only while a gate is waiting on a person.
Every string these transcripts introduce, grouped by the command that prints it. Angle brackets are values filled in at runtime.

Desktop V2 labels its step 3 gate "Hard gate" yet offers "Always for prisma migrate here". Under the rule in this brief, a hard gate never offers it. I drew prisma migrate as an ordinary gate and used a delete outside the project as the hard gate. Which classification is right, and which surface changes?
Can a person choose Always here outside watch? The approve command has no way to say it. I left it interactive only rather than invent a flag.

A script calling approve on a hard gate is refused with 33, so a script can never be the person. Deny works from anywhere. Is a terminal attached to stdin enough proof of a person, or does a hard gate need a device credential with a decide scope as well?
When does send land: when the current tool call returns (drawn), or at the next turn boundary like a model change?
Does watch exit when the turn ends (drawn), or keep following later turns?
Reconnect attempts and backoff are not specified anywhere. I drew five attempts, doubling from 2s. The daemon side is also open: how long does it keep a result for a client that has not come back?
The receipt line "checkpoint ckpt_7f24 taken before it ran" depends on the per-approval checkpoint, which Desktop V2 marks as proposed. Drop the line until it ships?
Both layouts use · − … and B uses box drawing characters. What does the CLI print when the locale is not UTF-8, and is NO_COLOR honoured? Layout A survives both because every state is also a word.
The policy refusal says only an org owner can change the rule. Should it also name where, and does a solo account have an owner?
The exit code numbers are proposed. Which are frozen for 1.0, and is 130 right for Ctrl-C when the session keeps running?

session new returns once the daemon holds the session. watch is only a view onto it, so Ctrl-C leaves the session running. send reaches the agent when its current tool call returns.

Both fit 80 columns. Set the columns tweak to 72 or 60 to see the difference: A only loses right-aligned meta, while B's border wraps into noise. A also stays greppable in a CI log and keeps its meaning without colour, because every state is a word. B reads as a stronger interrupt, which the amber header line already gives A.

The client lost the daemon, not the work. A call in flight shows as unconfirmed until the daemon says otherwise. On reconnect watch replays what the daemon recorded. If the daemon has no result either, the turn stops rather than guessing.
